bug_semantics: When access control is on, is_path_trusted in scripts/iib/api.py decides whether a requested filesystem path is inside an allowed scanned directory by testing path.startswith(parent_path) (and the inverse parent_path.startswith(path) when the request is shorter). Neither comparison appends os.sep, so a sibling whose name merely shares the allowed prefix is treated as trusted: if /data/images is allowed, /data/images_private/secret.txt passes. get_file then calls check_path_trust and returns FileResponse of that path, disclosing files the confinement was meant to exclude. The check is live only when get_enable_access_control() is true (IIB_ACCESS_CONTROL=enable, or auto-true for WebUI share/ngrok/listen/server_name); otherwise every readable file is served regardless of this bug. The same-commit helper is_path_under_parents used os.path.commonpath correctly for cache, so the startswith gate was a distinct, weaker confinement.
flaw_origin: The prefix-without-separator startswith gate was first written in 5f98c26b86f7e6bc049131441dd3a6aa5c2f0670 ('Add access control to ensure data security', 2023-06-10) as the original body of is_path_trusted, together with get_enable_access_control and the check_path_trust call on /file. Immediate parent 684dcb63fae43ca8edefc3f98c9ee6b7f4845b75 has neither the function nor any startswith(parent_path) check. Later history only retargeted parent_paths (mem['all_scanned_paths']) and swapped os.path.normpath for to_abs_path; git log -L and blame at pre-fix 7b6a81bb74298204cada8a956fc1b0212cf50dfc still attribute if path.startswith(parent_path) to 5f98c26. Copy-move blame (-C) of nearby try/except lines lands on 2f2e1d2942548f9b0b9eba2742ff91149409c787 need_cache, which used os.path.commonpath, not startswith. July 2023 revert/un-revert (323cdaa / 7d49900) restored the same mechanism and are not a first-write.

reasoning: CVE-2026-77814 / GHSA-6p87-gwpg-qp8w is a real CWE-22 prefix-collision in is_path_trusted: startswith against an allowed parent without a trailing separator lets a same-prefix sibling directory satisfy the trust check, after which /infinite_image_browsing/file serves the file via FileResponse. CVE.org lists the record PUBLISHED; the GitHub advisory is not withdrawn. The smallest public first-write of that startswith gate is 5f98c26b86f7e6bc049131441dd3a6aa5c2f0670, which added is_path_trusted, check_path_trust on get_file, and get_enable_access_control in one single-parent commit. The immediate parent tree was grepped and lacks the function and the startswith(parent_path) comparison, so introducer_parent_absent is false. git log -L plus blame (with and without copy detection) show later commits, including a revert/un-revert pair, did not first-write the vulnerable comparison; they are therefore not the BIC. The commit is not a merge and has no reconstructable public squash members. It is an ancestor of affected v1.8.0 and of every earlier tag from v0.0.1; the fix is absent from v1.8.0 and present in v1.9.0. AI is judged only from that BIC commit object: human maintainer zanllp is both author and committer, there are no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailers, and the author is not a bot. A later AI-looking fixer (PR #969) does not reattribute the introducer. Verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
